title: ALMA Observations of Massive Clouds in the Central Molecular Zone: Jeans Fragmentation and Cluster Formation
question: Do massive CMZ clouds contain hidden early-phase fragmentation into cores, and is it consistent with thermal Jeans fragmentation and with forming Arches/Quintuplet-like clusters?

data.sensitivity: 40 uJy/beam rms (~60 near brightest Sgr C peak)

evidence.quote: We assumed $R$=100 and $\kappa_\nu$=0.899 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ (cite: ossenkopf1994).

what.value: Parent 0.2 pc core gas temperature 50–200 K and density 1e6 cm-3

evidence.quote: we adopt the characteristic gas temperature 50–200 K and gas density $10^6$ cm$^{-3}$ from those works.

external_data.citation: Lu et al. 2017; Lu et al. 2019a

what.value: H2O maser and UC HII region associations

evidence.quote: About 30 cores are spatially associated with H$_2$O masers ([1](#fig:cont)) or UC H ii regions (cite: lu2019a)

recipe.method: tclean with Briggs weighting, multiscale clean, self-calibration on Sgr B1-off and Sgr C
astrodendro dendrogram on non-PB-corrected images; leaves are cores; fluxes from PB-corrected images; drop leaves outside 30% PB response
key_parameters: min flux 4 sigma, min significance 1 sigma, min area = beam

recipe.method: Optically thin dust: M = R S d^2/(B(T) kappa); r=(A/pi)^0.5; n(H2)=M/(4 pi r^3/3)/(2.8 mH)
key_parameters: T_dust = 20 K, R = 100, kappa = 0.899 cm2/g, d = 8.178 kpc
assumptions: Optically thin dust, constant 20 K, gas-to-dust 100

recipe.method: MLE power-law fit of dN/dlogM with simultaneous lower bound (KS minimisation), plfit
MST of core positions, deprojected by 2/pi; compare with Jeans length and mass
key_parameters: Jeans: T 50–200 K, n = 1e6 cm-3, rho = n(H2) x 2.37 mH

evidence.quote: the 5$\sigma$ mass sensitivity is 0.3 $M_\odot$ per beam given a $T_\text{dust}$ of 20 K
The other three fittings reach similar values of $\alpha$ in the range of 1.00–1.07.
The lower bound of all fittings is found to be around 5 $M_\odot$
In the three clouds, the most frequent separation is $\sim$$10^4$ AU.
The derived Jeans length is (1.0–1.9)$\times$$10^4$ AU.
This is generally consistent with the Jeans mass of 3–25 $M_\odot$.
the 90% completeness limit is estimated to be $\sim$2 $M_\odot$ for the 20 km s$^{-1}$ cloud

answer_key.quantity: CMF index, flux-dependent T_dust, fixed lower bound 1 Msun

evidence.loc: Appendix: Impact of Varying Dust Temperatures

not_stated_but_needed: Image size and phase centres per field
Which execution blocks and calibrators were used; flux calibrator and flux uncertainty
Exact astrodendro call details beyond min_value/min_delta/min_npix
Primary beam correction details and mosaic pointing layout
score_reason: Imaging and dendrogram parameters are given and the catalog is online, but several imaging details and the full pipeline scripts are missing.
rediscovery_reason: The project code is given, the recipe is mostly specified, and the results are numeric (core counts, alpha, separations).
